Short answer genetics.

Long answer is that our ancestors had a full body covering of hair. As we evolved less and less body hair was apparently a sexually successful trait, probably having to do with heat management. Hair on the head is more than likely just selected for sexual attraction. A full beard is usually seen as manly because you have to high testosterone levels to produce one, so it's an indicator of sexual fitness. How we evolved it, I have no clue.

Basically the way the your hair is distributed and the resulting growth patterns are a genetic lottery. The large overall trends in the species is through natural selection over 10s to 100s of thousands of years. All of them can be boiled down to selected as sexually attractive or successful in one way or another. For a more in depth answer you might be better off in a science subverse.

FSH or folicle stimulating hormone is the one responsible for hair growth at the onset of puberty. It figures in both the male and female hormone cycle and is produced in the pituatry gland. It has an effect on egg production in females and sperm production in males thus larger concentrations are found in those areas (and thus increased hair growth there). Mind you this is me recalling my A level biology from over 10 years ago so if there are any ammendments to be made please let me know!

Hair in general can be used to take sweat away from the skin so it can be theorised that male pubic hair acts as a 'wafting' system for the pheromones secreted in sweat.

We evolved the ability to grow hair back when we weren't so great at wearing clothes, so the hair kinda grew where we needed it most. Head: To keep our heads warm. We lose a lot of body heat through our heads.
Face: Eyebrows and eyelashes are to keep our eyes protected, and facial hair is for protecting our faces in fights.
Chest and torso: For protecting us, once again, from physical damage but to also retain body heat and to protect us from the sun (at least a little).
Crotch: Our nether regions are kind of sensitive, so it'd be kinda nice to have some sort of layer between our junk and the elements, right?

So anyway, that's just my two cents.
